mission: Establish Ben's restlessness and the persistent wrongness in the Force that no one else seems to notice at the same intensity
why_now: Opening scene — introduces protagonist, central mystery, and emotional baseline before the plot launches
conflict: Ben feels something wrong in the Force but cannot articulate it to anyone, and the Order treats it as background noise from recent crises
turning_point: Ben acknowledges privately that the wrongness has a quality he recognizes from his years around Jacen and Abeloth — something structural, not emotional
opening_hook: The Force has been off-key for three months, and Ben Skywalker is the only person in the Temple who can't stop hearing it
closing_hook: Luke appears in the doorway with a datapad and an expression Ben knows means a mission
emotional_trajectory: Restless unease -> frustrated isolation -> reluctant hope

stakes.personal: Ben's sense of his own Force perception — is he reliable or traumatized?
stakes.interpersonal: His distance from other Knights who don't share his concern
stakes.external: The wrongness itself — something is happening to the Force

setting: Jedi Temple, Coruscant — meditation chamber, late evening
sensory_details: Temple hum of ambient Force presences; the wrongness like a note played slightly flat in an orchestra only Ben can fully hear; cool stone under his hands
promises_planted: The wrongness has a source Ben will find (PP01)
Ben's Skywalker shadow — he measures himself against legacy (PP21)
notes: Establish Ben's Lie: self-reliance as safety. He's handling the wrongness alone because that's what Skywalkers do. Internal monologue should be sharp, self-aware, slightly defensive.
